name: Suzaku
summary: Historical Japanese–US X-ray satellite whose XIS blank-sky spectra have been used to search for radiative dark-matter decay in the Galactic halo.
detection_principle: X-ray imaging spectroscopy measures diffuse backgrounds, jointly modeling instrumental lines and astrophysical backgrounds to search for narrow spectral lines.

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: NASA lists the mission end as 2015-09-02.

collaboration.name: Suzaku collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

results.summary: No significant narrow dark-matter line was found; sterile-neutrino parameters were constrained.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
